newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world July sugar ends down, specs sell spread.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world July sugar ends down, specs sell spread.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled lower in July and firmer in the back months, with speculative selling in the July/October spread accounting for the bulk of today's trade, dealers said.
Trade buying in the switch, which has supported July at a premium for the past several sessions, dried up once the spread hit par.
The spread settled at a 0.07-cent premium in October, compared with a 0.02 cent discount on Monday.
Steady trade buying was also noted in the March/May switch, dealers said.
While prices are seen holding to their recent range ahead of the July expiry on Monday, October could dip under 11.00 cents briefly amid weakness in the spread.
Major support was pegged at the recent low of 10.96 cents in October. A move below that price could trigger sell stops and prompt another round of speculative liquidation, traders said.

The spot July contract closed 0.05 cent lower at 11.08 cents per lb, traded 11.15 to 11.05 cents. October settled 0.04 cent higher at 11.15 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.04 to 0.10 cent firmer.
Open interest in the benchmark October contract rose by 534 lots to 85,415 lots as of Monday. July lost 8,533 lots, putting open interest in the front month at 30,958 lots.
An estimated 24,468 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Monday's official 32,815 lots.
